written: So here's the sequence itself, and your lecturer said it out loud: learn this, because it will be asked. Picture the action potential sweeping down the axon and arriving at the terminal. That depolarisation opens voltage-gated calcium channels in the presynaptic membrane, and calcium rushes in — outside the cell there's far more of it than inside, so the gradient is huge. That calcium influx is the key step: it converts an electrical signal into a chemical one. It makes synaptic vesicles — little membrane sacs already loaded with neurotransmitter — fuse with the presynaptic membrane and dump their contents into the cleft. That fusion is exocytosis. Then the neurotransmitter diffuses across the cleft, binds to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, and you get a postsynaptic potential. Electrical in, chemical across the gap, electrical out. Before we move on — how would you run that sequence back to me in your own words?

written: So you know the picture already: two neurons almost touching, with a tiny gap between them called the synaptic cleft, about twenty nanometres wide. The question is, how does a signal jump that gap? Here's the sequence, and it's worth learning in order. First, an action potential arrives at the axon terminal. That depolarisation opens voltage-gated calcium channels, and calcium rushes in from outside, because its concentration out there is far higher than inside. Second, that calcium influx is the trigger — the step that converts an electrical signal into a chemical one. It makes synaptic vesicles, little membrane sacs loaded with neurotransmitter, fuse with the presynaptic membrane and dump their contents into the cleft. That's exocytosis. Third, the transmitter diffuses across the cleft and binds to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, which produces a postsynaptic potential. The lecturer's warning is worth hearing: no calcium, no release — the action potential still arrives and nothing happens. Before we move on, how would you say the sequence back to me in your own words?
